title: Why Tourists Love Foreign Supermarkets
paragraphs: You're traveling somewhere new, and you make a list of all the things you want to see: a famous museum, an old castle, a beautiful beach — and a local supermarket!
Many people love visiting foreign supermarkets when they travel. A 2025 survey by Hilton hotels found that 77% of travelers enjoy going to grocery stores when they're abroad.

Earlier this year, Finnish supermarket chain K-Supermarket became the first in the world to officially list some of its supermarkets as tourist attractions on Tripadvisor. And in Japan, tourists love convenience stores so much that trying their snacks and drinks has become part of the travel experience!
So, what's the appeal of foreign supermarkets?
For one, foreign supermarkets offer items that people wouldn't normally find back home — new chip flavors, different types of skincare products, all sorts of candy bars.
People may also find products they normally buy at home at cheaper prices, because they're local to the place they're visiting.
And sometimes, even if you can get the same snack at home, it seems to taste better abroad.

Speaking with the BBC, psychologist Charles Spence explained something called the "Provençal Rosé Paradox" — whereby a wine that tastes amazing on a sunny holiday may not seem as good when you drink it at home on a rainy day.
The same can be said for food: where you eat it can be almost as important as what you eat.
Another reason is that people are increasingly looking for local, authentic experiences when they travel, instead of being caught in tourist traps.
That doesn't mean they don't want to visit historical sites — but they may also want to see how locals actually live.
"Monuments reveal how a country remembers its past, but a supermarket shows how it lives today," BBC journalist Dayna Camilleri-Clarke writes.
And finally, eating out for every meal can get expensive, so people might also visit supermarkets to save money while traveling!
